decisions.title: Proposal: move fraud scoring to a streaming model
decisions.statement: Fraud scoring would move from nightly batch to a streaming model on Kafka.
decisions.rationale: Would cut chargebacks from same-day card testing attacks.
decisions.sourceSnippet: Proposal: we will move fraud scoring to a streaming model, pending a cost review.

decisions.title: Refunds over €5,000 need a second approver
decisions.statement: Any refund above €5,000 requires approval from a second person in Finance Ops.
decisions.rationale: Control requested by the auditors after the Q2 review.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided that refunds above €5,000 need a second approver from Finance Ops.

decisions.title: Adopt OpenTelemetry for tracing
decisions.statement: New services emit traces with OpenTelemetry. Vendor-specific tracing agents will not be added.
decisions.rationale: Avoids lock-in and lets SRE change backends.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided to standardise on OpenTelemetry. No vendor-specific tracing agents in new services.

decisions.title: Mobile SDKs support the last two major OS versions
decisions.statement: The iOS and Android SDKs support only the current and previous major OS version.
decisions.rationale: Older versions are under 2% of payment volume.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We agreed to support only the last two major OS versions in the mobile SDKs.

decisions.title: Feature flags are removed within 30 days of full rollout
decisions.statement: A feature flag must be deleted within 30 days after it reaches 100% rollout.
decisions.rationale: Stale flags caused the wrong fee table to load in May.
decisions.sourceSnippet: Going forward, we will remove every feature flag within 30 days of full rollout.

decisions.title: Extract reporting from the merchant dashboard
decisions.statement: Reporting is extracted into its own service; the rest of the merchant dashboard stays in the Rails application.
decisions.rationale: Report generation was starving the web workers at month end.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided to extract reporting into its own service. This supersedes ADR-005 for reporting only.

decisions.title: Checkout calls to the acquirer have a 3 second timeout budget
decisions.statement: Every call from checkout to an acquirer must have a 3 second timeout and at most one retry.
decisions.rationale: Unbounded waits pile up connections and take down checkout for everyone.
alternativesRejected: Per-acquirer custom timeouts set by hand
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided that all acquirer calls from checkout get a 3 second timeout budget with a single retry.

decisions.title: Keep authentication in-house; do not move to Firebase
decisions.statement: We will not move customer authentication to Firebase Auth. Identity stays on our own auth service in the EU region.
decisions.rationale: Data residency: our banking partners require EU customer identity data to stay in EU-controlled infrastructure, and Firebase Auth could not guarantee single-region storage for all identity metadata.
alternativesRejected: Auth0 hosted in the US region
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided NOT to move authentication to Firebase. EU customer identity data must stay in EU-controlled infrastructure.

decisions.title: Use Kafka for payment events
decisions.statement: Payment events are published to Kafka. We will not add new RabbitMQ queues.
decisions.rationale: One event backbone, replayable history for reconciliation.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We chose Kafka as the single event backbone. No new RabbitMQ queues will be added.

decisions.title: All payment API writes must be idempotent
decisions.statement: Every write endpoint in the payments API must accept an Idempotency-Key header and be safe to retry.
decisions.rationale: Double charges during retries were our most expensive class of bug in 2025.
decisions.sourceSnippet: Going forward, we will require an Idempotency-Key on every write endpoint in the payments API.

decisions.title: Card data never touches our servers
decisions.statement: We will not store or log raw card numbers (PAN). Card capture goes through the tokenisation vault only.
decisions.rationale: Keeps most services out of PCI DSS scope.
alternativesRejected: Encrypting PANs in our own database
decisions.sourceSnippet: We will never store or log raw card numbers. All card capture goes through the tokenisation vault.

decisions.title: PostgreSQL is the system of record for the payments ledger
decisions.statement: All money movement is recorded in PostgreSQL. We will not use DynamoDB or any eventually consistent store for the payments ledger.
decisions.rationale: Double-entry bookkeeping needs serializable transactions and foreign keys.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided that PostgreSQL is the only system of record for money movement. DynamoDB was rejected for the ledger.

decisions.title: Monolith first for the merchant dashboard
decisions.statement: The merchant dashboard stays a single Rails application. We will not split it into microservices this year.
decisions.rationale: A team of six cannot operate ten services.
decisions.sourceSnippet: We decided to keep the merchant dashboard as one Rails application.

decisions.title: Deploy freezes on the last two business days of each month
decisions.statement: We will not deploy to production on the last two business days of the month, except for incident fixes.
decisions.rationale: Month-end settlement runs are the highest-risk window for merchants.
decisions.sourceSnippet: The team agreed that there are no production deploys on the last two business days of each month.
